class ConfigPreviewTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(self.temp.name) / "releases.json"
        self.desk = ReleaseDesk(self.path)
        self.desk.add("1.0.0", [{"category": "Added", "text": "One"}])
        self.desk.add("2.0.0", [{"category": "Fixed", "text": "Two"}])

    def preview(self, base, target, current, base_version="1.0.0", target_version="2.0.0"):
        return self.desk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base, target, current)

    def test_report_shape_and_disjoint_changes_both_kept(self):
        result = self.preview(
            {"port": 80, "timeout": 30},
            {"port": 8080, "timeout": 30},
            {"port": 80, "timeout": 60})
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"baseVersion", "targetVersion", "canApply", "config", "conflicts"})
        self.assertEqual(result["baseVersion"], "1.0.0")
        self.assertEqual(result["targetVersion"], "2.0.0")
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"port": 8080, "timeout": 60})
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"], [])

    def test_same_field_changed_differently_conflicts_and_keeps_current(self):
        result = self.preview({"port": 80}, {"port": 8080}, {"port": 9000})
        self.assertFalse(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"port": 9000})
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"], [{
            "path": "/port",
            "base": {"present": True, "value": 80},
            "target": {"present": True, "value": 8080},
            "current": {"present": True, "value": 9000}}])

    def test_current_matching_target_is_kept_even_when_plan_changes(self):
        result = self.preview({"port": 80}, {"port": 8080}, {"port": 8080})
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"port": 8080})

    def test_current_matching_base_adopts_target(self):
        result = self.preview({"port": 80, "name": "old"}, {"port": 8080, "name": "new"},
                              {"port": 80, "name": "old"})
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"port": 8080, "name": "new"})

    def test_additions_and_deletions(self):
        added = self.preview({"a": 1}, {"a": 1, "n": 2}, {"a": 1})
        self.assertEqual(added["config"], {"a": 1, "n": 2})
        removed = self.preview({"a": 1, "g": 9}, {"a": 1}, {"a": 1, "g": 9})
        self.assertEqual(removed["config"], {"a": 1})
        # The current side deleting the same field independently is fine.
        both_removed = self.preview({"a": 1, "g": 9}, {"a": 1}, {"a": 1})
        self.assertTrue(both_removed["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(both_removed["config"], {"a": 1})
        # Independently adding the same key to different values conflicts.
        both_added = self.preview({}, {"k": "T"}, {"k": "C"})
        self.assertFalse(both_added["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(both_added["config"], {"k": "C"})
        self.assertEqual(both_added["conflicts"][0]["path"], "/k")

    def test_plan_unchanged_fields_keep_current_including_local_edits(self):
        result = self.preview({"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 9, "b": 2, "mine": True})
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"a": 9, "b": 2, "mine": True})

    def test_nested_objects_preview_per_subfield(self):
        base = {"db": {"host": "h", "port": 1, "keep": "x"}}
        target = {"db": {"host": "h2", "port": 1, "keep": "x"}}
        current = {"db": {"host": "h", "port": 2, "keep": "x"}}
        result = self.preview(base, target, current)
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"db": {"host": "h2", "port": 2, "keep": "x"}})
        # Same nested subkey changed differently conflicts at the subpath only.
        clash = self.preview({"db": {"port": 1}}, {"db": {"port": 2}}, {"db": {"port": 3}})
        self.assertFalse(clash["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(clash["config"], {"db": {"port": 3}})
        self.assertEqual([entry["path"] for entry in clash["conflicts"]], ["/db/port"])

    def test_whole_subobjects_added_or_removed_never_split(self):
        adopted = self.preview({}, {"o": {"x": 1}}, {})
        self.assertTrue(adopted["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(adopted["config"], {"o": {"x": 1}})
        clash = self.preview({}, {"o": {"x": 1}}, {"o": 2})
        self.assertFalse(clash["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(clash["config"], {"o": 2})
        self.assertEqual([entry["path"] for entry in clash["conflicts"]], ["/o"])
        delete_vs_edit = self.preview({"o": {"x": 1}}, {}, {"o": {"x": 2}})
        self.assertFalse(delete_vs_edit["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(delete_vs_edit["config"], {"o": {"x": 2}})
        self.assertEqual([entry["path"] for entry in delete_vs_edit["conflicts"]], ["/o"])

    def test_arrays_and_type_changes_are_whole_conflicts(self):
        array_clash = self.preview({"l": [1]}, {"l": [1, 2]}, {"l": [1, 3]})
        self.assertEqual([entry["path"] for entry in array_clash["conflicts"]], ["/l"])
        self.assertEqual(array_clash["config"], {"l": [1, 3]})
        # An array the current side did not touch adopts the target array.
        array_adopt = self.preview({"l": [1]}, {"l": [1, 2]}, {"l": [1]})
        self.assertTrue(array_adopt["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(array_adopt["config"], {"l": [1, 2]})
        type_clash = self.preview({"a": 1}, {"a": {"x": 1}}, {"a": 2})
        self.assertEqual([entry["path"] for entry in type_clash["conflicts"]], ["/a"])
        self.assertEqual(type_clash["config"], {"a": 2})

    def test_missing_differs_from_null(self):
        # Target drops a null the current side never changed: deletion adopted.
        result = self.preview({"a": None}, {}, {"a": None})
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {})
        # Target adds a null onto a current config without the field.
        result = self.preview({}, {"a": None}, {})
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"a": None})
        # Current holds null while the target changes the base scalar: conflict.
        result = self.preview({"a": 1}, {"a": 2}, {"a": None})
        self.assertFalse(result["canApply"])
        side = result["conflicts"][0]
        self.assertEqual(side["current"], {"present": True, "value": None})

    def test_conflict_sides_only_carry_value_when_present(self):
        result = self.preview({"a": 1}, {"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 1, "c": 3})
        # Plan adds b, current adds c: no overlap, both enter the preview.
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3})
        clash = self.preview({"a": 1}, {}, {"a": 2})
        entry = clash["conflicts"][0]
        self.assertEqual(set(entry), {"path", "base", "target", "current"})
        self.assertEqual(entry["target"], {"present": False})
        self.assertNotIn("value", entry["target"])
        self.assertEqual(entry["base"], {"present": True, "value": 1})

    def test_conflicts_sorted_by_unicode_code_point(self):
        base = {"": 0, "a~b": 0, "a/b": 0, "z": 0, "A": 0, "中": 0}
        target = {k: 1 for k in base}
        current = {k: 2 for k in base}
        result = self.preview(base, target, current)
        paths = [entry["path"] for entry in result["conflicts"]]
        self.assertEqual(paths, sorted(paths))
        self.assertEqual(len(paths), 6)
        self.assertEqual(paths[0], "/")

    def test_unrelated_changes_still_enter_config_with_conflicts(self):
        result = self.preview(
            {"port": 80, "timeout": 30, "note": "x"},
            {"port": 8080, "timeout": 30, "note": "y"},
            {"port": 9000, "timeout": 60, "note": "x"})
        self.assertFalse(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(result["config"], {"port": 9000, "timeout": 60, "note": "y"})
        self.assertEqual([entry["path"] for entry in result["conflicts"]], ["/port"])

    def test_same_version_and_reverse_order_allowed(self):
        base = {"a": 1}
        target = {"a": 2}
        same = self.preview(base, target, dict(base), "1.0.0", "1.0.0")
        self.assertEqual(same["config"], {"a": 2})
        reverse = self.preview(target, base, dict(target), "2.0.0", "1.0.0")
        self.assertEqual(reverse["config"], {"a": 1})

    def test_invalid_and_unknown_versions(self):
        for base, target in ((None, "1.0.0"), ("v1", "1.0.0"), ("1.0", "1.0.0"),
                             ("1.0.0.0", "1.0.0"), ("01.0.0", "1.0.0")):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.desk.preview_config(base, target, {}, {}, {})
        for base, target in (("9.9.9", "1.0.0"), ("1.0.0", "9.9.9")):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                self.desk.preview_config(base, target, {}, {}, {})
            self.assertEqual(str(caught.exception), "unknown release")

    def test_all_three_configs_validated(self):
        good = {"a": 1}
        for bad in (None, [], "x", 1, True, {1: "x"}, {"a": float("nan")}, {"a": object()}):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

        raw = b'{"1.0.0": [], "1.0.0": []}'

    def test_readonly_inputs_store_and_files_untouched(self):
        before, mtime = self.path.read_bytes(), self.path.stat().st_mtime_ns

An invalid or unknown version, invalid store content, a non-object root, a non-string key, a non-JSON value (including non-finite numbers) or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level (the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere), printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown.

`ReleaseDesk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config)` is a read-only three-way preview that checks whether applying the base→target plan would overwrite independent edits already present in the current configuration, and `python3 release_desk.py preview-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json` reads all three configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, just like `diff-config`. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files and follow the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `diff_config`, and nothing — the passed objects, the files, the store — is modified and no directory is created.

For each field, the plan is the base→target change. A field the plan does not change keeps its current presence state and value, including independent current edits and current-only fields. When the plan does change a field, a current value equal to the target is kept, a current state equal to the base adopts the target (whole additions and deletions included), and any other state is resolved field by field only when the field exists on all three sides and all three values are objects; otherwise it is one conflict at that path whose preview keeps the current field's presence state and value. Whole subobject additions and deletions, arrays (never split) and type changes are always judged as a whole, so a whole-value conflict never lists subpaths; every other non-conflicting change still enters the preview. Equality uses the `diff_config` rules, including `null` differing from a missing field and two missing fields being equal. The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config` and `conflicts`: `config` is the complete previewed object, `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and each conflict holds only `path` plus `base`, `target` and `current`, each of those holding a `present` boolean and a `value` only when present. `path` uses the same JSON Pointer escaping as `diff-config`, and `conflicts` is sorted by path in Unicode code point order. For example, a target that changes the port while the current config only changes a timeout keeps both changes, while both sides changing the same port to different values keeps the current port and reports a `/port` conflict.

An invalid or unknown version, invalid store or a configuration violating the existing config validation rules raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory.

content.text:
Done. Three-way config preview is implemented, tested, and documented.

## What changed

**`release_desk.py`**
- **`ReleaseDesk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config)`** — read-only three-way merge. It validates both version strings, all three config objects (existing `_validated_config` rules), then reads and validates the whole store and checks both versions are registered; same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed. Returns exactly `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config`, `conflicts`.
- **`_preview_config_values`** core resolver — per field:
  - plan unchanged (base==target) → keep current state, including current-only edits/deletions;
  - plan changes it and current==target → keep; current==base → adopt target (including whole add/delete);
  - otherwise recurse only when the field exists on all three sides **and** all three are objects; anything else is one whole-field conflict (arrays never split, type changes and added/removed subobjects judged wholesale, no subpaths). Conflict fields keep current presence/value in `config`.
- Presence-aware equality (`_present_equal`) reuses `_json_values_equal`: missing ≠ `null`, two-missing is equal. Each conflict side is `{"present": bool}` plus `value` only when present; conflicts sorted by path in Unicode code-point order with existing JSON Pointer escaping.
- **`preview-config` CLI command** taking base/target versions and three UTF-8 JSON file paths, using `--store`, with duplicate-key/encoding/syntax errors funneled through the existing handler → single-line `error`, exit 2; valid previews (even with conflicts) → single-line result, exit 0. Nothing is written and no files or directories are created.

**`test_release_desk.py`** — new `ConfigPreviewTests` (20 tests): disjoint/same-field merge, adds/deletes, nested per-subfield merge, whole subobjects, arrays, type changes, null-vs-missing, sorting, conflict shape, validation of all three inputs, invalid/missing store, read-only/untouched inputs, and CLI success/error paths.

**`README.md`** — two new paragraphs documenting the API/command semantics and error handling; `preview_config` added to the API list and "config preview" to the test list.

All 144 tests pass (124 pre-existing + 20 new), and all existing public entry points are unchanged.
